property_summary: If the caller has a balance >= MinSum and >= _am, after a successful Collect(_am) the caller's balance should decrease by _am.

After any sequence of public calls ending with a successful Collect, the total supply of ether in the contract (balances mapping plus contract balance) must remain unchanged when the caller already had sufficient balance.
After any successful Collect call where the caller's balance is at least MinSum and _am, the caller balances[msg.sender] must be the original balance minus _am.
After Collect(uint _am) succeeds, balances[caller] must never exceed its value before the call.
The total Ether held by the contract (sum of all balances plus contract balance) must never increase due to a Collect call.
After any sequence of operations ending with Collect(uint), the balance of any address never decreases below MinSum minus the maximum withdrawal amount.

After Collect(uint256) is called, the caller's balance in the reference always decreases only when the balance is at least MinSum, but in the mutant it decreases when the balance is less than MinSum. The rule is that the balance of the caller after Collect is either unchanged or is less than the balance before Collect by exactly the amount withdrawn, and additionally, if the balance after Collect is less than the balance before Collect, then the balance before Collect was at least MinSum.
After Collect is called, if the caller's balance decreased, then the caller's balance before the call was at least MinSum.
After any call to Collect, the balance of any address never increases.
After a call to Collect(uint256), the caller's balance can only decrease if before the call it was at least MinSum.
After any call to Collect, the caller's balance never exceeds its pre-deposit balance.
After Collect, the total sum of all balances in the map is non-negative and does not exceed the sum of all deposits made via Deposit.
After any Collect call, the caller's balance is less than or equal to the sum of its previous deposits (i.e., the balance never increases due to a Collect).
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance is the same as if deposits subtract from balance (i.e., the balance does not increase due to a Collect in the buggy version).
After any call to Collect, the sum of all balances in the mapping is invariant with respect to deposits and withdrawals (i.e., total deposit amount equals total balance plus total withdrawn).
If Collect succeeds (does not revert), then balances[caller] + _am before collect equals balances[caller] after collect, ignoring the balance update in Deposit.

After calling Collect(uint256), the caller's balance in the buggy version is unchanged (since Deposit never updates balances), but in the reference version it decreases by _am if the conditions are met.
After any call to Collect(uint256), the caller's fee in C is not transferred; instead, the caller's balance after Collect is the same as before, regardless of the Collect outcome.
After any call to Collect(uint256), the sum of all balances in the contract is unchanged if the call reverts, otherwise it decreases by _am.
After Collect(uint256) successfully transfers funds, the caller's balance in the contract must decrease by exactly _am.
After a successful Collect call, the emitted log entry's Val field equals the collected amount, and MinSum remains unchanged.
After calling Collect, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged from its initial value (set via SetMinSum).
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, MinSum equals the value set by the last SetMinSum call (or the default if never called).
After a Collect call, MinSum retains the value last set by SetMinSum, not zero.
After SetMinSum is called, MinSum equals the value passed to SetMinSum, not zero.
After a call to Collect(uint256), the contract balance should be reduced by exactly the collected amount if the collection succeeds.
After any Collect call, the total balance of the contract plus sum of all user balances equals the original contract balance plus all deposits, regardless of MinSum.
After a Collect(uint256) call that does not revert, either the sender's balance has decreased or the contract's balance has decreased, ensuring no phantom increase in total value.
The total contract balance plus sum of all user balances is invariant and equals initial balance plus all deposits regardless of SetMinSum value.
After any Collect call, the contract's total balance plus the sum of all user balances is at most the deposit balance sum plus any external funds sent to the contract.
After a Collect call the Log address is never the zero address if the caller has enough balance and collects at least MinSum.
After a successful Collect call, the LogFile address is never the zero address
After a successful Collect call that sends ether, the LogFile address is not the zero address.
The LogFile address stored in the contract must be the address passed in SetLogFile, not the zero address.
After a successful Collect call, the LogFile address is the address that was set by SetLogFile.
After a Collect call that does not revert, the caller's balance never exceeds its previous balance minus the withdrawn amount.
The sum of all balances plus the contract's ether balance never exceeds the total ether ever deposited (i.e., the contract's balance plus all recorded balances is non-decreasing).
After a Collect call that does not revert, the total ether received by the contract (its balance plus the sum of all recorded balances) does not decrease.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance is always less than or equal to its previous value.
After a Collect call that does not revert, the contract's total ether balance plus the sum of all recorded balances is non-decreasing.
The balance of msg.sender after Collect should never exceed the initial balance, because Deposit only adds funds.
After Collect, the contract's own address balance must be at least the sum of all deposits minus the sum of all collects.
After collect, the total contract balance plus all user balances is invariant (deposits only add, never subtract).
After Collect, the total contract balance plus sum of all user balances equals the total Ether received by the contract.

After Collect, the caller's balance in the mapping should be greater than or equal to the amount collected, but in the buggy version a subtraction during Deposit can make it artificially low, leading Collect to revert unexpectedly.
After Collect(uint256) completes, the length of LogFile History has increased by 1.
After Collect(uint256) completes, the last LogFile History entry's Data field equals 'Collect'.
After Collect(uint256) completes, the balance of msg.sender plus the amount collected equals its previous balance.
After Collect(uint256) completes, the msg.sender's balance in the contract's mapping is reduced by exactly _am.
After a successful Collect call, the length of the LogFile History array has increased by exactly 1.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance must not increase; the rule checks that balances[msg.sender] post-collect <= balances[msg.sender] pre-collect.
After Collect, the caller's balance cannot increase above the initial balance plus the amount _am.
After Collect(_am), the caller's balance decreases by at most _am, i.e., balances[msg.sender] after Collect >= balances[msg.sender] before Collect - _am.
After Collect(_am), the caller's balance in the contract must not decrease by more than _am.
After Collect, the total sum of balances (sum over all addresses) must not increase beyond its pre-collect value.
After Collect(uint256), the caller's balance decreases by the collected amount.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance in the contract is its previous balance minus the collected amount.
After Collect(uint), the contract's balance decreases by exactly _am when the call succeeds.
After a successful Collect(uint256) call, the contract's total ether balance decreases by _am.

After a successful Collect(uint _am) call, the balance of msg.sender in the contract's balances mapping is the sum of the previous balances after Collect and the amount _am if the operation had been subtraction.
After a call to Collect(uint256), the caller's balance always decreases by at most the amount they deposited.
After Collect(uint256) reverts if _am exceeds the caller's balance, the caller's balance remains unchanged.
After Collect(uint256) succeeds, the caller's balance remains non-negative.
After Collect(uint256) completes without revert, the caller's balance in the contract is decreased by exactly _am.
After Collect(_am) reverts when _am > balance, caller's balance stays unchanged.
